title: Automatic Replenishment Debits — Paystride Instant Pay Disbursement Service Treasury Desk Tool Reference
content:
## The automatic replenishment debit

This rule settles the automatic replenishment debit that Paystride pulls from the employer's bank account under its authorization on a Paystride Instant Pay Disbursement Service. When automatic replenishment is on, which only tiers that allow automatic replenishment permit, a prefund balance below the alert level on file triggers one replenishment debit of at least the tier's smallest automatic replenishment debit, sized under this rule, booked as one deposit made by ACH debit authorization and marked as an automatic replenishment.

A replenishment debit is not pulled until the alert level on file stands at or above the replenishment floor. While the alert level on file stands below the replenishment floor, no replenishment debit is pulled.

A replenishment debit is sized only after the ledger carries the platform fee of every completed billing month whose fee debit day has come. While any such month has no platform fee entry on the service's ledger, the debit is not sized.

The debit falls due when the balance is below the alert level on file on a service with automatic replenishment on.

## Pulling the debit

The debit is booked with `book_replenishment_debit_b3fe8e59`, an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it and then calls it.

**Capability.** It pulls an automatic replenishment debit from the employer's bank account under its standing authorization for an Instant Pay Disbursement service. One call books one prefund deposit dated today, made by ACH debit and marked as an automatic replenishment, and raises the service's prefund balance by the amount; the employer sees the debit on its ledger at once, and the money can be paid out once the tier's ACH availability period has passed.

### Parameters

- `disburse_service_id` — the reference number of the employer's Instant Pay Disbursement service, read from the service record returned by the service lookup (identifier).
- `amount` — the amount to debit, in US dollars as a positive number with exactly 2 decimal places; a value with more decimals is rounded half up to the cent before booking.

### Return

- A one-line confirmation naming the new ledger entry reference (text), the service reference (text), the entry date (YYYY-MM-DD), the ordinal of the deposit among the service's deposits booked that day (integer), the amount debited (US dollars, two decimals) and the prefund balance after the debit (US dollars, two decimals). The entry reference being present means the debit was booked.
- A message beginning "Not booked" means the amount was not greater than zero and nothing changed.

### Contract illustration (hypothetical values)

On a day when the service already has one deposit booked, an `amount` of 3700 books a debit of 3700.00 reported as deposit 2 of the day; an `amount` of 0 returns a message beginning "Not booked".
